# `hs-run review-pr` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run review-pr` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown_forge` | The remote names neither github nor gitlab, so no CLI can be chosen. Ask which forge this is; do not guess, because a wrong-forge command is worse than a question. | `references/forge-detection.md` |
| `cli_unavailable` | The forge was identified but its CLI is not installed. Nothing about the PR has been read yet — this is a machine that cannot ask, not a PR that has no answer. | `references/forge-detection.md` |
| `cli_unauthenticated` | The CLI is installed and refuses to answer without credentials. Kept separate from "still running" on purpose: an auth problem polled as if it were slow CI spins until the ceiling and then reports a timeout. | `references/forge-detection.md` |
| `ci_check_failed` | The forge CLI itself failed — a network, permission or API error, not a failing check. The envelope's warnings carry what it said; nothing has been learned about the PR's CI either way. | `references/forge-detection.md` |
| `no_checks_found` | The forge reports no checks at all. An empty result, never a passing one: it means either no PR/MR exists for what was asked, or this project runs no CI — two different situations that both leave the review with no CI evidence. | `references/forge-detection.md` |
| `ci_done` | Every check reached a terminal state and every one of them passed. That is a fact about CI, not a verdict on the PR: the diff has still not been read, and green CI is the weakest evidence in the review because it only says the tests that exist did not fail. | `claim-verification`, `anti-tautology-detection`, `scoring-rigor-contract`, `references/mandatory-gates.md`, `references/anti-ai-slop.md` |
| `ci_failed` | A check finished and did not pass. Whether that failure is transient is a judgment this verb never makes and never authorises — rerunning to make a deterministic failure disappear is the move these rules exist to stop. | `verification-mechanism`, `auto-decision-ledger` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `error` | The invocation itself was wrong — a missing or malformed flag. Nothing was read and nothing was decided; fix the command line and re-run. |
| `ci_timeout` | The polling ceiling was reached with checks still unfinished. This is where the loop hands back to a human — escalate rather than starting a fresh count, which is the one move that makes a ceiling meaningless. |
| `ci_pending` | At least one check is still running. Run the printed command again after the stated wait; the CLI owns the round count and the ceiling, so neither is re-derived by hand. |
